text:
Ivan Barbashev spent part of the season off the top line, and the Las Vegas Review-Journal put the result plainly on Nov 16: "Experiment over: Barbashev back on Golden Knights' top line." Vegas takes 58.8% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, more than seven points better than without him.

He has 16 points in 24 games, 12 of them assists, which is who he is: a forward who makes the line around him work. His four goals on 5.4 expected are a touch light, nothing alarming.

The highlight was Nov 11 against Utah, two goals in a win, one of them a candidate for goal of the year by the team's own billing. The low point came five nights later, a roughing penalty after the whistle late in a loss to Vancouver that Jesse Granger of The Athletic called a bad one.

Evolving-Hockey had him at 2.2 wins above replacement last season, 42nd among forwards, while noting his teammates are strong enough to flatter raw on-ice numbers.

What to watch: he has gone four games without a point and Vegas has lost four straight. The top line needs his assists back.
headline: Barbashev is back where the experiment ended
